title: Provider & module compatibility ledger and automated smoke/rollback playbook
creator: Priya Singh
description: Create a single-source compatibility ledger that maps supported combinations of Terraform module versions, provider versions (AWS, Azure, GCP, HashiCorp), and runtime kernels for Private (VPC) deployments. Complement the ledger with an automated smoke/rollback playbook: CI gating checks, post-upgrade health probes, canary rollout plan for module/provider changes, and documented rollback commands and recovery metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility ledger published as markdown + CSV in infra/docs with clear major/minor compatibility rules
Automated CI gate that fails on unsupported module+provider combinations (unit/integration checklist)
Canary upgrade procedure defined and validated on staging (scripts + Terraform workspaces)
Post-upgrade health-check suite (API smoke, KV-cache sanity, tail latency check) implemented and auto-run after terraform apply
Rollback playbook documented and exercised in 2 runbook drills with run results recorded
Documentation links added to oncall runbook and release notes template
steps: Inventory current module/provider usage across active VPC clusters (query IaC state + terraform statefiles)
Collect known-good combos from ops (last 6 months) and recent incident reports
Define semantic compatibility rules (major bump = breaking unless shimmed; patch = safe when provider changelog OK)
Author compatibility matrix CSV with columns: module, module_version, provider, provider_version, notes, tested_on
Implement CI check (github action) that consumes CSV and fails PRs violating matrix
Create terraform canary workspace and automated smoke tests (using terratest and shell probes)
Add post-upgrade probes into deployment pipeline: health endpoints, latency SLO checks, KV cache key counts
Write rollback scripts: terraform state rollback steps, provider plugin pinning, steps to re-apply previous module version
Run two simulated upgrades on staging and document timings/failure modes
Publish final ledger + playbook to infra/docs and link from console upgrade flow
comments: 2025-02-12 - Priya Singh: Kickoff meeting notes attached; agreed to prioritize AWS provider variants first due to highest usage.
2025-02-14 - Diego Martinez: Initial inventory script (scripts/collect_tf_state.sh) pushed to infra/tools and ran against 42 clusters; results in /tmp/tf-inventory-20250214.csv
2025-02-17 - Aisha Patel (SRE): Proposed health probes: /health, /metrics (prometheus), kv-cache:active_keys. Added thresholds for tail latency: p95 < 120ms.
2025-02-21 - Security review notes: need KMS key rotation considerations when rolling provider versions that touch KMS resources. Marked security_review_required = true.

2025-02-25 - Review feedback from Eng Leads: Add explicit downgrade strategy for provider plugins that require re-initialization (terraform init -upgrade) and include provider_lockfile snapshots in PRs.
2025-02-28 - Diego Martinez: CI gate prototype added in infra/.github/actions/compat-check; currently tests against a sample CSV. Next: integrate with PR template and block merge on mismatch.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict pinning reduces blast radius but increases maintenance cost; chosen approach: pin major versions in ledger and recommend minor/patch pinning via provider_lockfile for pipelines.
Decision log: use progressive canary (10% of clusters) then 50% then full if health metrics stable for 30m per stage.
Known limitation: GCP provider 4.x has a state migration caveat; ledger entry will mark 4.x as 'requires migration-check' until module update available.
Incident link: ENG-39815 referenced for state drift observed during a previous provider upgrade—lessons incorporated into post-upgrade probes.
